patch.value: Ordinary presence join storms fail readiness before 3000 subscribers

Follow-up to pm-web-h4vh. With unchanged production queue, stall, authorization and pool bounds, a sixteen-slot ordinary ramp returned an SSE project-verification HTTP 500 around 1800 subscriptions; an eight-slot diagnostic disconnected readers around 1400 subscriptions. No measured mutations had started in either failed setup. Preserve the failed sequences in docs/capacity/2026-10-20-fanout-exploratory.json. The fan-out comparison defers incremental presence only in its test preload, then requires every real full-roster receipt before measuring established subscribers. This does not certify ordinary join storms. Profile roster generation/transport, membership reads, pool waits and safe verification error categories; repair the ordinary join path without weakening authorization or slow-viewer bounds.

Ordinary startup with no quiet-setup control reaches and retains 100, 1000 and 3000 distinct authorized subscribers on one project; every socket receives the complete final roster; mixed committed mutations retain zero loss and duplicates; normal release thresholds and queue/auth bounds remain unchanged.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: The final baseline ordinary ramp also failed before measurement, while the deferred-presence candidate held 3000 subscribers and delivered 150000 mutations exactly. An earlier baseline ordinary ramp succeeded, so readiness remains variable. Corrected test-preload registration order after archiving the data; the source-replacement regression fails on the old order. This only repairs comparison setup control. Production ordinary joining remains unresolved; retain the unchanged authorization, queue/stall and pool bounds in any follow-up.

value.text: Measuring ordinary authenticated join bursts with the existing disposable capacity fixture, production process and independent SSE readers. Extending the harness to sample readiness during admission and roster convergence for bursts of 100, 500 and 1000 up to 3000 subscribers. No quiet-setup interception; authorization and replay bounds remain required.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Exploratory unchanged-server burst-100 run reproduced a setup failure at 1397 opened streams: 41 failed readiness samples (39 HTTP 503, two client deadlines), readiness p99 1858 ms, event-loop p99 257 ms, peak server RSS 279 MiB. This first driver overallocated reader workers; correcting it to reuse four workers before the controlled before/after comparison. Candidate design coalesces roster updates into fixed one-second windows and yields bounded socket batches, refreshing authorization between batches while preserving replay cursors and byte/stall limits.

value.text: The controlled 1000-request baseline burst failed project verification before meaningful roster traffic (one opened reader, three readiness deadlines). Join setup now has bounded FIFO admission: up to eight concurrent initializations, reduced for smaller SQL pools, with 4096 pending slots and cancellation on socket close. Each admitted request retains all original authorization and cursor checks. Real HTTP admission regression passes 1/1 for overload, cancellation, idempotent release and responsive readiness.
